title: CSV sentinel values & noise scratchpad
summary: Scratchpad for heuristics to detect and canonicalize sentinel/malformed values in CSV exports before labeling. Focus: when to treat as missing vs noisy real value, and examples to add to the labeler guide.
content:
Context:
Quick notes while triaging labeling batches from billing and user-profiles exports. We see a lot of sentinel values used inconsistently across sources. Downstream labelers are confused (is "000-000-0000" a phone, or 'no phone'?) and automated dedup/validation scripts remove some things incorrectly. Aim: small set of deterministic heuristics + sampling rules to flag ambiguous cells for human review, and canonicalization rules for bulk cleanup when safe.

Observed sentinel patterns (examples from sample files):
- Explicit text: "NULL", "null", "N/A", "n/a", "none", "-", "--"
- Numeric sentinels: "-999", "99999", "0" (in some numeric-only fields), large placeholder dates like "9999-12-31" or epoch-ish "1970-01-01" used as "unknown"
- Padded zeros: phone "0000000000" or formatted "000-000-0000"
- Reused placeholders: email "no-reply@example.com" used for missing, or "user@localhost"
- Quoted empties: "" (two quotes), or string containing only whitespace ("  ")
- Mixed garbage: stray characters from encoding issues (e.g., BOM, �), control chars, accidental concatenation like "NULLN/A"
- CSV structural noise: unescaped newlines inside fields, extra delimiters in free-text columns, trailing commas creating extra empty cols

Heuristic proposals (early, conservative):
1) Normalization pass (LOW RISK):
   - Trim whitespace, remove surrounding quotes, collapse multiple spaces, normalize Unicode (NFC).
   - Lowercase for comparison against sentinel list (keep original as backup column _orig).

2) Sentinel canonicalization list (SAFE to treat as missing):
   - EXACT matches after normalization: "", "null", "n/a", "none", "na", "-", "--"
   - Common placeholder emails: "no-reply@%", "noreply@%" (treat as missing for email label extraction)
   - Date sentinels: 9999-12-31 and 1970-01-01 ONLY if column typed as date and distribution shows >95% of these as placeholders.
   - Numeric -999 / 99999 if numeric field and outlier compared to column percentiles (>99th or <1st) AND upstream docs mention sentinel usage.

3) Ambiguous cases (FLAG for human review):
   - A phone field == "000-000-0000" or all zeros: flag. Some customers actually use zeros as testing numbers.
   - "0" in numeric fields: depends on semantics (e.g., balance 0 is valid). Use schema if available.
   - Concatenated tokens like "NULLN/A": flag for manual correction if frequency low, otherwise bulk replace with missing if high frequency (>500k rows).

4) PII labeling implications:
   - If canonicalized to missing, do NOT label as PII.
   - If ambiguous (e.g., "no-reply@example.com" could be a real domain), preserve original and attach tag "sentinel-suspected" for downstream models.
   - For phone/email columns used in PII training, build a filtered sample of flagged vs canonicalized rows to estimate false positive rate.

5) Sampling & scope rules for labeler queues:
   - If field has >0.1% ambiguous entries, create a labeler micro-batch (n=200) sampled stratified by source_system and region to surface systemic sentinel use.
   - Provide labelers with a short checklist: compare normalized value, check adjacent columns for related data (e.g., email domain or account id), consult the _orig column.

Edge-case examples to include in labeling guide (copy these into the PRD):
- "--" in free-text address line — sometimes used when address unknown vs intentional dash.  Checklist: if other address fields empty, mark as missing.
- "1970-01-01" in birthday — often default epoch; if many birthdays are concentrated on that date, treat as missing.
- "no-reply@domain.com" repeated with many accounts — treat as missing for contact purposes, but keep raw for fraud signals (tag).
- "000-000-0000" — if source_system == "legacy-telephony" and test_account == true -> likely test number; else flag.
- Strange non-ascii noise: "John�Smith" — UTF replacement char; try to run unicode-fix heuristics then flag if still suspicious.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Add canonicalization transform in the ingestion pipeline with safe fallback: write transformed -> new field '<col>_clean' and keep '<col>_orig'.
- Expose a "sentinel_reason" tag with small enum: [canonicalized, flagged, unchanged] and free-text for human_notes.
- Provide small metrics dashboard: percent canonicalized per column, examples (top 20 unique) and how many flagged.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we treat "0" as missing for numeric IDs? (ask product: are zeros used as real ids?)
- How do we encode provenance so customers can opt out of canonicalization? Need opt-out flag in connector config.
- Build a regex library for common sentinels per column type (email, phone, date, numeric, free-text). Draft regex list next.

Quick draft regex ideas (to refine):
- email sentinel: ^(no-?reply|noreply|user|unknown)(@|%40).+  (case-insensitive)
- phone zeros: ^[\s\-\()]*0{7,}[\s\-\)]*$  (tolerant of formatting)
- date sentinel: ^(1970|9999)-\d{2}-\d{2}$
- numeric sentinel: ^-?9{2,,}$ or ^-999$ (explicit)

Manual labeler instructions (one-pager):
- When a value is canonicalized to missing, mark "confirmed placeholder" or "false positive" if it appears to be real.
- If unsure, choose "flag for engineering" and add short note of why (e.g., "looks like test account").
- Always check neighboring columns (account_id, created_at, region) for context.

Next steps (short):
- Ship normalization + canonicalization to staging for one customer export (billing CSV) and measure how many cells changed. (Owner: Liam)
- Prepare labeler micro-batch template & small annotation guide (Owner: Priya)
- Draft regex library and unit tests (Owner: me - Aisha)

Notes to self: keep conservative. We break downstream if we over-canonicalize. Prefer flagging to deleting. Save examples that cause disagreement and add to a curated list for periodic re-runs.

End of scratchpad.
